content:
Happy to announce the formalization of Schmidt's Subspace Theorem in https://github.com/rwst/Subspace-Theorems . The roadmap is also a PR in Tau Ceti (please review if you want it there). The roadmaps follow Bombieri-Gubler, Schmidt and several other works.

The comparator challenge includes:

  • Siegel's Lemma in 7 variants
  • Roth's Theorem in 7 variants
  • Subspace Theorem in 7 variants
  • Evertse's counting of the subspaces, 5 variants

All in all 87 kLOC, done by Opus 5 without subagents in about 60 hours over 11 days. Have fun.

Was it $100000 of API costs or a $20 subscription or something in between?

Edit: TIL how frustrating it is to search a formalization.yaml file on mobile. Does the GitHub app have no search functionality for files? Looked on a browser and had issues with the long lines. But I think the answer is "subscription"

Nice! I guess it should be easy to obtain a proof of the LeanEval statement from this? That would be the first public solution to the challenge.

Worth noting there is also Faltings’ product theorem presented in the slides https://pub.math.leidenuniv.nl/~evertsejh/14-bonn.pdf of Evertse that gives a new proof and strong quantitative versions of the subspace theorem.

Nice! I guess it should be easy to obtain a proof of the LeanEval statement from this? That would be the first public solution to the challenge.

Worth noting there is also Faltings’ product theorem presented in the slides https://pub.math.leidenuniv.nl/~evertsejh/14-bonn.pdf of Evertse that gives a new proof and strong quantitative versions of the subspace theorem.
